legalIndex.metaTitle: Legal Literacy Index — every country scored | BasicLaw
legalIndex.metaDescription: An educational, shareable ranking of 195+ jurisdictions across seven heuristic dimensions. Not an authoritative legal assessment — see methodology.
legalIndex.banner: Educational index. Not an authoritative ranking. Methodology below.
legalIndex.heroSubtitle: Every country in our library, scored on seven dimensions from the public data we already publish. Built to spark curiosity and conversation — not to declare legal truth.
legalIndex.searchPlaceholder: Type a country name or code…
legalIndex.methodologyIntro: These scores are deterministic heuristics applied to BasicLaw’s own dataset: legal-system labels, languages, constitution adoption/amendment years, plain-language summaries, key principles, and source links. No LLM runs at scoring time; nothing here is a substitute for legal research or expert judgment.
legalIndex.weightsLine: Overall score = weighted average: accessibility 16%, plain-language constitution 14%, rights protection 18%, judicial independence 16%, citizen empowerment 10%, constitutional clarity 14%, cross-jurisdiction interoperability 12%.
legalIndex.dim_accessibility: Accessibility — language access proxies plus how navigable the labelled system appears from metadata (e.g. common law vs religious law labels).
legalIndex.dim_plainLanguage: Plain-language constitution — recency of adoption/amendments, number of key principles, and whether our summary length looks informative without being overwhelming.
legalIndex.dim_rightsProtection: Rights protection — keyword breadth in our summary and principles (life, liberty, expression, equality, due process, privacy, assembly, etc.).
legalIndex.dim_judicialIndependence: Judicial independence — legal-system label plus explicit mentions of independent courts or separation of powers in principles, with a very light regional prior.
legalIndex.dim_citizenEmpowerment: Citizen empowerment — participation keywords (referendum, petition, etc.) and proxy for modern charters; we do not parse full referendum rules from source law.
legalIndex.dim_constitutionalClarity: Constitutional clarity — amendment freshness, how many URLs we list, and a penalty for uncodified systems in our data.
legalIndex.dim_crossJurisdiction: Cross-jurisdiction — static EU/Commonwealth membership lists plus a coarse region baseline (treaty/bloc density proxy only).
legalIndex.limitation1: Scores reflect our JSON summaries, not verified compliance or court practice.
legalIndex.limitation2: Regions like EU/Commonwealth are rough proxies; many treaties and bodies exist beyond those labels.
legalIndex.limitation3: Grades are opinionated cut-points on heuristic points — useful for discussion, not league tables for policy.
legalIndex.detailMethodologyBody: Each paragraph below is generated only from BasicLaw’s public fields (legal system, languages, constitution summary, key principles, adoption/amendment years, and URLs we list). It is not a review of court practice or compliance.

homeFaq.title: What people ask before they trust us

i1.q: Is BasicLaw a substitute for a lawyer?
i1.a: No. BasicLaw is educational. We help you understand what the law says, but only a licensed lawyer in your jurisdiction can give legal advice on your specific situation. We tell you when to find one.

i2.a: All 195 internationally recognised countries are in the library, with a plain-language summary of the constitution, key principles, and links to the official text. The interactive assistant is rolling out country by country — start with the United States, Ghana, and Nigeria today.

i3.q: Where do the constitutions come from?
i3.a: We summarise from the official primary source where available, and link to the Comparative Constitutions Project (constituteproject.org) for the full English text. Constitutional law changes — always verify against the official version before relying on a provision.

i4.a: Each constitution entry includes the year of adoption and the most recent amendment we are aware of. Where a constitution has been suspended, contested, or replaced by a transitional charter, we say so directly in the summary.

i5.a: The Constitution Library and most of the Q&A is free to read. Pro and Pro+ tiers add document analysis, multi-jurisdiction comparison, saved chats, and priority models — see the pricing page for details.

i6.q: Can I use BasicLaw answers in court or in a filing?
i6.a: No. BasicLaw answers are designed to help you understand legal concepts and frame the right questions to ask a lawyer. They should not be cited as legal authority or used as a substitute for legal representation.

i7.q: How do voice (microphone) and read-aloud features handle my audio?
i7.a: Voice typing and “read aloud” use your browser’s Web Speech API. BasicLaw does not store microphone recordings on our servers for speech-to-text when you use that browser feature; processing may occur on-device or via your browser vendor’s speech service (for example Google in Chrome), per your browser’s policies. Read-aloud is generated locally by your browser or operating system — the audio is not uploaded to BasicLaw. You can review the short privacy section on our privacy page and adjust permissions in your browser settings.

privacyPage.voiceBody: When you use voice input with the Web Speech API, your microphone audio is processed by your browser and may be sent to your browser vendor’s speech services (for example Google in Chrome), not to BasicLaw’s servers for transcription. BasicLaw does not record microphone audio on its servers for that flow. Read-aloud uses your device or browser speech synthesis; the text you ask to hear is not sent to BasicLaw for audio generation. Check your browser and OS privacy settings if you need to limit cloud speech features.
privacyPage.generalBody: BasicLaw is an educational tool. Review each feature’s in-product notices for how prompts and documents are processed.

pressPage.metaDescription: Logos, boilerplate, founder bio, and press contact for BasicLaw.
pressPage.heroSubtitle: For journalists, educators, and integration partners.
pressPage.blurb50: BasicLaw is a plain-language constitution and rights library covering every country, with chat, audits, and citizen questions — educational only.
pressPage.blurb100: BasicLaw turns constitutions and core legal topics into clear, jurisdiction-aware guides, chat answers, and contract audit tools. It is civic education software, not a law firm, and complements professional counsel.
pressPage.blurb250: BasicLaw helps people orient themselves in unfamiliar legal systems: country constitutions in plain language, guided citizen questions, an Ask assistant grounded on curated sources, and red-flag contract audits. Coverage spans nearly two hundred jurisdictions with transparent limitations — the product is educational infrastructure, not personalised legal advice. Journalists can use this kit for boilerplate, logos, and factual stats; partners should treat listings as independent of any endorsement by BasicLaw.
